guide.summary: The request fits Notion's OAuth integration model for customers in other workspaces. The supplied snapshots document OAuth 2.0 for OAuth and public integrations, with each user authorizing individually, and token exchange at the token endpoint. The least-privilege capability for reading existing shared page titles and content is Read content, which the snapshots describe as covering reading existing content and not updating or creating pages. Read content is mapped to the single read action. Registration details, provider review, marketplace distribution and customer-admin approval are not covered by the supplied snapshots and remain unknown.

findings.title: OAuth 2.0 is the documented access model for OAuth integrations
findings.detail: The documentation states that OAuth integrations and public integrations use the OAuth 2.0 protocol. Each customer who connects authorizes individually, and only that authorized user can interact with or share pages with the connection, so each customer workspace or member must complete the auth flow.

findings.title: Read content capability for reading existing shared pages
findings.detail: Read content gives a connection access to read existing content in a Notion workspace. The documentation says a connection with only this capability can call read endpoints such as Retrieve database but not Update database. Read content is needed to read titles and content of shared pages. It does not permit creating or updating pages, and access is limited to pages the customer explicitly shares.
findings.appliesWhen: The app reads titles and content of pages a customer shares with the integration.

Continue listing block children until has_more is false
Done when: Requests are repeated with returned next_cursor values until a response has has_more false. Only GET requests are recorded in the outgoing request log.
